## Discovery & Translational Science

* **TransMap uncovers trans-QTL architecture and neuron-to-glia signaling in aging human brain** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26367384)
  * Introduced TransMap, a computational framework integrating multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization, achieving 9.2–36.7% higher discovery power than existing methods.
  * Applied to brain tissue samples from the ADSP FunGen-AD consortium (average N = 476), yielding variant annotations with 2.75–2.88× heritability enrichment across 57 complex diseases and traits.
  * Mapped 49,532 trans-regulatory events and demonstrated an asymmetric regulatory axis where neuronal cis-regulatory signals drive downstream trans-regulatory responses in glia.

* **Single-nucleus profiling of human carotid plaques maps driver mechanisms of plaque vulnerability** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.07.26367408)
  * Analyzed 53 symptomatic and asymptomatic carotid plaques using snRNA-seq (19,100 nuclei) and scRNA-seq (68,983 cells), uncovering shifts toward terminal states in osteochondrogenic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and CD4⁺ T cells alongside endothelial cell (EC) EMT transitions.
  * Nuclear profiling revealed a depletion of RGS5-positive vascular wall fibroblasts in symptomatic lesions.
  * Integration with GWAS data prioritized higher TWIST1 expression in ECs, lower GUCY1A1 expression in fibroblasts and macrophages, and higher MRAS expression in T cells as driver mechanisms.

* **ShortKit-ML detects shortcut learning risks in frozen medical imaging embeddings** [arXiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.29.26352053)
  * Developed ShortKit-ML, a calibrated linear probe evaluating conditional dependence between frozen embeddings and sensitive demographic attributes (sex, age, race) to assess shortcut potential.
  * Across CheXpert and MIMIC-CXR encoders, probe scores correlated with true positive rate gaps in confounded downstream classifiers (Spearman ρ = 0.60), confirming that head refitting on group-balanced data outperforms embedding-level mitigations.

* **SP1-CD44 axis regulates pentose phosphate pathway metabolism and gemcitabine sensitivity in pancreatic cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42998852/)
  * Identified that SP1-CD44 signaling modulates pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-associated metabolic flux in pancreatic cancer cells.
  * Disruption of this pathway directly influences cellular sensitivity to gemcitabine chemotherapy.

* **Plasma proteomic Mendelian randomization prioritizes therapeutic targets in age-related macular degeneration** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42998155/)
  * Applied a multi-omics Mendelian randomization framework to the human plasma proteome to identify causally linked therapeutic targets for age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

* **Antidepressant maintenance trial design validity supported by remitter enrichment simulations** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.02.25337182)
  * Simulated maintenance/discontinuation trials in major depressive disorder using STAR*D symptom data and pooled parameters from nine clinical trials.
  * Selection of acute-phase remitters increased the average drug benefit 1.7-fold (from 1.75 to 2.91 Hamilton Depression Rating Scale points), explaining the observed maintenance effect size without compromising internal validity.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **Psilocybin achieves rapid antidepressant response without altering SV2A synaptic density** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.26367247)
  * A pre-registered [¹¹C]UCB-J PET sub-study in 35 patients with moderate-to-severe recurrent MDD randomized to single-dose psilocybin (25 mg) or niacin (100 mg) evaluated SV2A binding as a marker of synaptic density.
  * Despite rapid clinical improvement, psilocybin produced no group-level increase in hippocampal or frontal cortex SV2A binding relative to niacin at 15 days post-dose.
  * Higher baseline SV2A binding (Vₜ) significantly predicted greater clinical improvement at Day 8 and Day 15 in the psilocybin cohort.

* **Phase 1 trial tests oral fecal microbiota capsules combined with immunotherapy as solid tumor maintenance** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42998537/)
  * Initiated a single-arm, dose-escalation Phase 1 study evaluating fecal microbiota capsule transplantation combined with first-line maintenance immunotherapy in patients with malignant solid tumors.

* **Extended aldosterone synthase inhibition yields disease remission in primary hyperaldosteronism** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2611265?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Longitudinal trial data showed that extended targeted inhibition of aldosterone synthase led to sustained suppression of hormone output and clinical remission of primary hyperaldosteronism.

* **Cangrelor compared with crushed ticagrelor in AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42998670/)
  * Presented results from the randomized, double-blind DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial comparing intravenous cangrelor against oral crushed ticagrelor in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Novartis Lp(a) antisense pelacarsen fails to reduce cardiovascular events in pivotal trial** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2610159?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial results showed that pelacarsen significantly lowered circulating lipoprotein(a) levels but failed to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) compared to placebo.
  * The disconnect between robust Lp(a) biomarker reduction and lack of clinical benefit presents a major challenge to the Lp(a) hypothesis in cardiovascular risk reduction [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/07/aha-conference-news-novartis-lp-a-pelacarsen-heart-disease-trial-mystery/?utm_campaign=rss).

* **[Big Pharma]** **Novo Nordisk anti-IL-6 antibody ziltivekimab fails in Phase 3 ZEUS trial** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2612126?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Interleukin-6 inhibition with ziltivekimab did not achieve a statistically significant reduction in cardiovascular events in high-risk patients with atherosclerotic disease in the Phase 3 ZEUS trial.
  * Investigators noted that while the trial failed its primary endpoint, anti-inflammatory mechanisms in cardiovascular disease remain under active exploration [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/07/aha-2026-conference-novo-nordisk-zeus-trial-ziltivekimab-results/?utm_campaign=rss).

* **Intensive blood pressure targets yield mixed outcomes in stroke and diabetes trials** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2612922?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Two landmark randomized controlled trials evaluated intensive systolic blood pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes and those with prior ischemic stroke [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2612924?af=R&rss=currentIssue).
  * Intensive blood pressure management presented substantial operational and implementation challenges in clinical practice alongside variable efficacy profiles across cohorts [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/07/new-studies-on-blood-pressure-management-aha-conference-news/?utm_campaign=rss).

* **[Biotech]** **Pan-PPAR agonist chiglitazar reverses molecular insulin resistance despite BMI gain** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.26367120)
  * In an integration of 835 type 2 diabetes patients across two Phase 3 trials (ChiHOPE cohort), 53% of chiglitazar-treated patients with baseline HOMA-IR resolved IR criteria compared to 29% on placebo and 32% on sitagliptin.
  * Multi-omic plasma HOMA-IR scores fell significantly under chiglitazar (marked by lower proteoglycan 4 and higher glycine/glutamine) despite concurrent weight gain.

* **Prehospital extracorporeal life support fails to improve survival in refractory cardiac arrest** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2602919?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * A randomized trial evaluating prehospital initiation of extracorporeal life support (ECLS) for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest showed no significant survival advantage compared to standard advanced cardiac life support.

* **RCT evaluates statin discontinuation in primary prevention for older adults** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2606634?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Assessed safety and clinical outcomes associated with discontinuing statin therapy in older adults without established cardiovascular disease.

## Business & Strategy

* **Big Pharma M&A reaches $332 billion since 2023 targeting revenue loss from patent cliffs** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/paras_biotech/status/2119333837113364928)
  * Financial analysis from Truist indicates approximately $332 billion in biopharma M&A transactions since 2023 has been deployed to acquire late-stage assets replacing revenue lost to patent expirations [@paras_biotech].

* **Cardiovascular trial failures highlight clinical translational gaps in AI drug discovery models** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/08/heart-drug-failures-lessons-for-artificial-intelligence-from-aha-conference/?utm_campaign=rss)
  * Late-stage trial failures reported at the American Heart Association conference emphasize ongoing difficulties in translating AI-predicted therapeutic targets into human clinical efficacy for complex cardiovascular indications.

## Public Health & Policy

* **BIO sues HHS to block international reference pricing pilot for Medicare** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/07/bio-sues-to-block-globe-drug-pricing-model/?utm_campaign=rss)
  * The Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO) filed a lawsuit seeking to halt a Medicare pilot program ("Globe model") that ties domestic drug reimbursement to prices in peer countries.
  * The legal action challenges the Most-Favored-Nation pricing framework, arguing administrative overreach and potential harm to early-stage biopharma investment.

* **Caregiver reliance on LLMs for pediatric diabetes risks improper insulin dosing advice** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.26367316)
  * Evaluated four programmatic LLM endpoints and two chat interfaces responding to caregiver questions on pediatric hyperglycemia in type 1 diabetes.
  * LLMs frequently provided insulin dosing advice without warning users to account for insulin-on-board (IOB), exposing patients to potential severe hypoglycemia.

* **FitNMF pipeline enables de novo viral variant detection from longitudinal wastewater sequencing** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.26367358)
  * Developed FitNMF, an integrated matrix factorization model that reconstructs mutational signatures, relative abundances, and fitness advantages of emerging viral variants directly from wastewater NGS data.
  * Validated across six Swiss wastewater treatment plants (2021–2024), demonstrating accurate de novo variant tracking without requiring clinical genomic reference databases.

* **17-year survey reveals persistent drug use disparities by sexual identity in England** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26367385)
  * Analysis of Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Surveys (2007–2024, N = 21,861) showed past-year drug use among sexual minority adults (24.9% in 2024) remained double that of heterosexual adults (11.6%; adjusted OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.4–3.4).

* **Post-flood rainfall surges drive dengue transmission dynamics in Sindh, Pakistan** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26367382)
  * Epidemiological modeling of dengue incidence in Sindh, Pakistan (2020–2025) linked post-2022 flooding to post-monsoon case spikes, showing a 1-month lagged rainfall increase correlated with higher incidence (IRR = 1.008, 95% CI 1.003–1.012, p = 0.002).

* **Qualitative study of FDA Advisory Committees highlights public participation structural gaps** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42998121/)
  * Analyzed public speaker involvement during FDA Advisory Committee meetings, identifying operational barriers to integrating patient and public perspectives into formal regulatory evaluations.

***

**Worth watching:** The simultaneous Phase 3 failures of Novartis's pelacarsen and Novo Nordisk's ziltivekimab at AHA will likely prompt a strategic re-evaluation of late-stage cardiovascular pipelines targeting secondary biomarker reduction (Lp(a) and IL-6/inflammation) without clear proof of MACE reduction.

- Biology & Health
    - [How to effectively train your abdominal muscles | Jeff Cavaliere, M.S.P.T., C.S.C.S.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drDjOsO9-Cw) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Identifies junk volume as a major mistake in resistance training and examines what differentiates productive repetitions from wasted ones.
        - Details strategies for active training around a partially torn labrum and rotator cuff, positing that complete rest can impede recovery.
        - Highlights the necessity of dedicating more targeted training focus to calves, glutes, and smaller stabilizing muscles.
        - Outlines midlife indicators requiring modifications to training programs, such as joint soreness, fatigue, and irritability.
